home.seoTitle: Remote Valley OS — Open Innovation for the World's Toughest Environment
home.seoDescription: An open-source blueprint for innovation in remote regions. 5 pillars: trash-to-filament, water purification, food production, EV logistics, mesh networks. Field-tested in Jumla, Nepal.
home.heroTitle: Open Innovation for the World's Toughest Environment
home.heroText: An open-source blueprint for innovation in remote regions. Born from years spent in the Himalayas tackling real problems — plastic waste, contaminated water, food insecurity, isolation, and lack of connectivity.
home.pillarsText: Every pillar is designed, prototyped, and field-tested in real remote conditions. All designs are open source on GitHub.

pillars.title: Trash → 3D Filament
pillars.desc: Turning Himalayan plastic waste into recycled 3D printing filament for remote manufacturing.

pillars.title: Water Purification
pillars.desc: Low-cost, low-maintenance filtration for glacial melt and contaminated high-altitude sources.

pillars.title: Food Production
pillars.desc: High-altitude greenhouses, indigenous seed banks, and hydroponic systems for remote communities.

pillars.title: EV Logistics Network
pillars.desc: Electric vehicle charging stations every 50km, creating a sustainable Himalayan transport corridor.

pillars.title: Mesh Communication
pillars.desc: Decentralized peer-to-peer mesh network — no towers, no cellular, just resilient connectivity.

home.ctaText: If it works in Jumla, it works anywhere. Explore the board, apply for a residency, or contribute on GitHub.

jumla.seoTitle: Jumla Field Study & Residency Program | Remote Valley OS
jumla.seoDescription: Apply for the Jumla Residency — prototype open-source solutions for remote communities in one of the toughest environments on earth. Karnali Province, Nepal.
jumla.heroText: In the remote highlands of Karnali Province, at 3,000 meters elevation, Jumla is our living laboratory. A feasibility assessment conducted in May 2026, using environmental analysis and persona-based simulations.
jumla.whyP1: Jumla District is one of Nepal's most remote regions. Accessible only by small aircraft or a multi-day 4WD journey from the nearest paved road. No grid electricity. Intermittent mobile coverage. Winters that drop to -10°C.
jumla.whyP2: This is precisely why we work here. Jumla concentrates every problem the Remote Valley OS is designed to solve — plastic waste, contaminated water, food insecurity, energy poverty, lack of connectivity, and extreme isolation.
jumla.whyP3: The founding insight: If a solution works in Jumla, it will work in any remote community on Earth. The Himalayas are our proving ground.
jumla.findingsText: This assessment used environmental analysis and persona-based simulations based on published data — not live community workshops. Findings are directional, not definitive. Proper field studies with real community participation should be conducted before deployment.
jumla.residencyP1: The Jumla Residency brings engineers, designers, educators, and builders to live and work alongside the community. You will prototype real solutions, train local operators, and leave knowledge behind permanently.
jumla.residencyP2: Every resident follows a non-negotiable process: Build → Document → Train → Test. A system is not complete until three local operators can pass blind troubleshooting without assistance.
jumla.applyText: Email residency@mountaineer.fi with your background, a project idea, preferred duration, and any questions. We review applications with a committee that includes community representatives.
jumla.followText: Watch our team build, test, and iterate in Jumla. Every prototype, every failure, every breakthrough — documented openly on GitHub.

rvos.seoTitle: Remote Valley OS — Open Source Blueprint | Architecture & GitHub
rvos.seoDescription: The full open-source system architecture behind Remote Valley OS. Sensor ingestion, local LLM, offline-first design, and 5 interconnected modules. Fork on GitHub.
rvos.heroText: A system-of-systems integration layer connecting hardware, data, and people into one coherent infrastructure. Open source. Offline-first. Field-tested.
rvos.whatP1: Remote Valley OS is not an operating system in the Windows/Linux sense. It is a system-of-systems integration layer — the middleware and tooling that connects five independent infrastructure modules into a unified, observable, and manageable whole.
rvos.whatP2: Each module works on its own. RV-OS makes them work together. The stack runs fully offline and syncs to GitHub when connectivity is available.
rvos.sensorText: Every module is instrumented with sensors that report operational data. A lightweight agent on each module cluster collects, timestamps, and stores data locally before relaying it over LoRa or MQTT to the central collector.
rvos.llmText: A small, locally-hosted language model runs on the hub server, powered by the micro-grid. It answers maintenance questions in the local language and English, walks operators through troubleshooting, and translates documentation — all fully offline.
rvos.offlineText: Every component runs fully offline. Internet is never required for operation.
rvos.ctaText: Star the repo, open an issue, submit a PR, or apply for the Jumla residency. Every contribution moves the mission forward.
